clue.text: RADA accepting one with initially no characteristics — except brilliance!

indicators.note: a drama school accepting someone takes them in, so one letter goes inside the school's name

parts.note: the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, a London drama school
Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the words that follow it

parts.note: the opening letters of no, characteristics and except

explanation.surface: A drama school takes on a student with no qualities at all, apart from sheer brilliance.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA takes I inside to make RADIA, and the initials of 'no characteristics except' complete RADIANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiance is a glowing, shining quality, a close synonym of brilliance in both literal light and personal sparkle.

clue.text: For example, Epsom doctor cures chorea (not hard)

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged
not hard says the abbreviation for hard must be removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, then H for hard comes out

explanation.surface: A medic in the town of Epsom heals a nervous twitching disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom looks like a town for the doctor to work in, but it stands for the famous racecourse there, home of the Derby. H is the pencil abbreviation for hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is a well-known English horse-racing venue, so it is an example of a racecourse.

clue.text: Perish, hurling something out of a mould

parts.note: to perish is to die
casting is throwing or hurling

explanation.surface: Someone dies flinging an object free of a mould.
explanation.definitionFit: A die-casting is a metal object made by forcing molten metal into a mould, so it comes out of one.

clue.text: Ancient Athenian room

definitions.meaning: first meaning: belonging to Attica or classical Athens
second meaning: a space just under the roof of a house

explanation.surface: A chamber in an old Greek house.
explanation.definitionFit: Attica was the region around Athens, giving the adjective, and a top-floor room under the roof is also called this.

clue.text: It's one's right politely to embrace single chap

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold inside one's arms, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: civilly means courteously
I is the Roman numeral one
a man's name standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: Someone insists they are entitled to politely hug an unmarried man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single chap' looks like a bachelor, but it splits into a one and a man's name; the pair go in just before the final letter of the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A civil liberty is a freedom the law guarantees to each citizen, such as free speech, so it is a person's right.

clue.text: Rattle strangely towards the end

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something begins to rattle oddly just as it nears the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Latter describes the second or later part of something, as in the latter half, so it means nearer the close.

clue.text: Saint revered in East

parts.note: august means venerable or revered
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A holy figure honoured in the eastern world.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustine of Hippo, and Augustine of Canterbury, are both canonised Christians, so the name denotes a saint.

clue.text: Players in corporate America

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows

parts.note: the end of corporate and the start of America

explanation.surface: Actors or competitors working for big American business.
explanation.definitionFit: A team is a group of players who play together on one side in a sport or game.

clue.text: Conservatives heard religious ceremony

indicators.note: heard says to go by how the word sounds, not how it is spelt

parts.note: political conservatives are called the right

explanation.surface: Tories listened to a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a formal ceremonial act, especially one prescribed by a religion, such as baptism.

clue.text: Oddly cursed, Evita returned, showing imagination

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of cursed

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the name is read from its end

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A disgruntled audience member grumbles as the musical Evita comes back on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Being creative means having or using imagination to make original things, so it equals showing imagination.

clue.text: Horrified to be outed in Armagh as traitor

indicators.note: the answer is brought out from inside the words that follow, sitting within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of Armagh, all of as and the start of traitor

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled to be exposed as a turncoat in Armagh, a town in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with shock and dismay, which is exactly the state of being horrified.

clue.text: Former Labour leader and Speaker making complaint, attacking the cloven-hoofed!

parts.note: Michael Foot led the Labour Party from 1980 to 1983
taken as written
the mouth is the organ that speaks

explanation.surface: A past Labour leader and the Commons Speaker grumble while laying into devils with split hooves.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S makes Speaker look like the Commons chair; here it is just the body part that does the speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Foot-and-mouth is a contagious viral disease of cattle, sheep and pigs, animals with divided hooves; complaint means illness.

clue.text: Risk nearly all before old respected state leaders — Kohl and Brandt, perhaps

indicators.note: nearly all means not quite the whole word, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: to chance something is to risk it
taken as written, then trimmed

indicators.note: leaders are the front runners, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the opening letters of old, respected and state

explanation.surface: Gambling nearly everything on reputable past heads of government, such as two German leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the A is dropped from the front of ALL, an unusual trim since nearly normally cuts the last letter. Kohl and Brandt were both Chancellors of West Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Helmut Kohl and Willy Brandt each served as Chancellor, the head of the German government, so they are examples of chancellors.

clue.text: Frenchwoman is below par: that's stunned absent lover

indicators.note: in a down answer, below means coming after, setting the order of the two pieces
absent says some letters are missing from the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
taken as written
a stud is a womaniser

explanation.surface: A woman from France feels below par, shocked that her lover has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking STUD from STUNNED leaves NNE. PAR, IS, IE and NNE join to make PARISIENNE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Parisienne is a woman from Paris, so she is one kind of Frenchwoman.

clue.text: Calm and untouchable dignity

parts.note: sedate means calm and unhurried
Eliot Ness led the Prohibition agents nicknamed the Untouchables

explanation.surface: Serene composure and incorruptible dignity.
explanation.walkthrough: Untouchable looks like an adjective; it is one of Eliot Ness's Untouchables, the famous 1930s Chicago lawmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedateness is a composed, staid and serious manner, which is a form of dignity.

clue.text: Loony losing head, say

indicators.note: losing its head means the word gives up its first letter

parts.note: nutter is British slang for a crazy person

explanation.surface: A madman who has lost his mind tries to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to speak or pronounce words aloud, the verb sense matching say.

clue.text: Uproar! Peer topped crooked businessman!

indicators.note: topped means having its top cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a racket is a loud noise
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Topped is also slang for killed, which the surface uses.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs a dishonest or illegal business such as extortion, so is a crooked businessman.

clue.text: Involved in TT race, I break down

indicators.note: things that break down fall apart, letting the pieces be reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A motorcyclist in the Isle of Man TT race complains of a breakdown.

explanation.definitionFit: Intricate means very complicated and detailed, one sense of involved, as in an involved plot.

clue.text: Protective lotion: empty can ensures problem

parts.note: the first and last letters of can
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Sunscreen is a cream or lotion spread on skin to protect it from the sun's ultraviolet rays.

clue.text: Heather and Mr Cantona argue at first

parts.note: Eric Cantona, the French footballer

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the opening letter of argue

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather starts a quarrel with the footballer Eric Cantona.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers, low evergreen shrubs of moorland.

clue.text: Ad-lib first part of excuse before rate rise

parts.note: the opening two letters of excuse
tempo is speed or rate
taken as written

explanation.surface: An improvised excuse offered before a pay or interest rate increase.
explanation.definitionFit: To extemporise is to speak or perform without preparation, which is what ad-libbing means.

clue.text: No mistake, I'm up for this drug

parts.note: O looks like a zero, nothing
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Opium is the narcotic drug made from the dried juice of poppy seed pods.

clue.text: Catch sight of English agent

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a secret agent is a spy

explanation.surface: Glimpsing a British secret agent.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to notice or see something, usually at a distance, a literary word for spot.

clue.text: Yearn to be seen in nylon garter

indicators.note: seen in says the answer can be spotted inside the letters that follow

parts.note: the end of nylon and the start of garter

explanation.surface: Someone longs to appear wearing a nylon garter.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn for it, both verbs of strong desire.

clue.text: Untidy person loves muddle, up to a point

parts.note: taken as written
a point of the compass: north

explanation.surface: A messy person enjoys disorder, but only to a degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muddle up' looks like one phrase; 'muddle' alone mixes the letters and 'up to' simply places the compass point after them.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloven is someone careless and dirty in appearance or habits, an old noun for a slob.

clue.text: Nude, I jiggled amidst one group of spectators

indicators.note: jiggled letters are shaken about, landing in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A naked performer wiggles in front of the crowd watching.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience is the assembled body of people watching or listening to a performance.

clue.text: Fermented milk finally curdling in your tea, we hear

what we hear is a sound, so the spoken words stand for letters that sound the same

parts.note: your tea run together, spoken quickly

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word after it

parts.note: the closing letter of curdling

clue.text: Rooms used by cruciverbalists?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the British dictionary favoured by crossword setters and solvers

explanation.definitionFit: Chambers are private rooms or lawyers' offices, and Chambers is also the publisher of the dictionary crossworders rely on.
